comments.author: Urs Schreiber
comments.markdown:
Excellent point. We have been discussing these situations elsewhere a fair bit, under the name “adjoint modalities” \[1\]. For notice that the \_other\_ two (co-)monads obtained from Σ ⊣ Const ⊣ Π are the the necessity- and the possibility modalities for the context type regarded as a type of possible worlds \[2\]. Introducing further adjoint triples to (homotopy) type theory (”cohesion”) turns out to make it a highly expressive language for geometry. Mike Shulman has formalized this in \[3\], using the native logical expression of adjunctions via “adjoint logic” \[4\].

\[1\] [https://ncatlab.org/nlab/show/adjoint+modality](https://ncatlab.org/nlab/show/adjoint+modality)  
\[2\] [https://ncatlab.org/nlab/show/necessity+and+possibility#InFirstOrderLogicAndTypeTheory](https://ncatlab.org/nlab/show/necessity+and+possibility#InFirstOrderLogicAndTypeTheory)  
\[3\] [https://ncatlab.org/nlab/show/cohesive+homotopy+type+theory#Shulman15](https://ncatlab.org/nlab/show/cohesive+homotopy+type+theory#Shulman15)  
\[4\] [https://ncatlab.org/nlab/show/adjoint+logic](https://ncatlab.org/nlab/show/adjoint+logic)
